content.user_title: Shape Rough Ideas Into Validated Designs
content.value_statement: Unclear requirements cause teams to commit too early and overlook important trade-offs. This skill turns rough ideas into validated designs through focused questions and structured comparisons.
actual_capabilities: Asks one focused question at a time to identify purpose, constraints, and success criteria.
Proposes two or three approaches with explicit benefits, drawbacks, and complexity.
Organizes architecture choices in comparison tables and weighted decision matrices.
Presents designs in short sections and requests validation after each section.
Revisits earlier phases when feedback reveals new constraints or gaps.
Produces designs covering architecture, data flow, errors, security, testing, and implementation priorities.
limitations: Does not implement code or execute an approved design.
Relies on user answers and available project context for accurate recommendations.
Does not replace specialist security, legal, compliance, or performance reviews.
Example architectures are illustrative and require validation against current systems and requirements.

use_cases.title: Clarify a product idea
use_cases.description: Turn an early concept into clear goals, constraints, success criteria, and a validated scope.

use_cases.title: Compare feature approaches
use_cases.description: Evaluate several delivery options and document the trade-offs before committing roadmap resources.

use_cases.title: Validate system architecture
use_cases.description: Develop architecture, data flow, error handling, security, testing, and rollout decisions through incremental review.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify an idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me refine this idea: [idea]. Ask one question at a time to identify the goal, users, constraints, and success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when an idea is still broad or incomplete.

prompt_templates.title: Compare approaches
prompt_templates.prompt: Explore [problem] for [context]. Propose three approaches, explain benefits, drawbacks, and complexity, then ask me to select one.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when several reasonable solutions may fit.

prompt_templates.title: Build a decision matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a weighted decision matrix for [decision]. Compare [options] using [criteria], explain assumptions, and recommend an option after gathering missing constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a decision that needs transparent evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a validated design
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a complete design for [system]. Review available project context, resolve unclear requirements, compare architectures, and present architecture, data flow, security, testing, and rollout incrementally.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for complex technical planning before implementation.

output_examples.input: I want to add authentication to my web application.
output_examples.output: First question: Which requirement matters most for your authentication design: server rendering, instant revocation, minimal infrastructure, or cross-device access?

output_examples.input: Compare polling, server-sent events, and WebSockets for a dashboard.
output_examples.output: The comparison covers update latency, implementation complexity, bidirectional needs, connection overhead, and scale. It recommends an option only after confirming traffic and interaction requirements.

output_examples.input: Design a reliable notification service for our product.
output_examples.output: The design is presented in validated sections: requirements, architecture options, selected components, data flow, failure handling, security, testing, rollout, and open questions.

best_practices: Share concrete goals, target users, constraints, and success measures.
Answer each focused question before requesting the next design phase.
Challenge assumptions and revise earlier decisions when new constraints appear.
anti_patterns: Requesting implementation before requirements and trade-offs are validated.
Choosing the first proposed option without comparing credible alternatives.
Treating example architectures as production-ready specifications without independent review.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before coding or implementation planning when requirements are unclear or several approaches may work.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It develops and validates the design that should guide later implementation.

faq.question: Why does it ask one question at a time?
faq.answer: Focused questions reduce ambiguity and let each answer shape the next decision.

faq.question: Can it compare technical architectures?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares two or three approaches using benefits, drawbacks, complexity, and relevant constraints.

faq.question: What does the final output include?
faq.answer: It can include architecture, components, data flow, error handling, security, testing, priorities, and unresolved questions.

faq.question: Can the process revisit earlier decisions?
faq.answer: Yes. New constraints or validation feedback can return the discussion to requirements or alternative selection.
